subject: Reasoning
topic: Puzzles — box/floor/linear arrangement with positional clues
description: Seating/stacking arrangement puzzles: box stacking (top/bottom), floor puzzles, linear row arrangements — standard IBPS PO/Clerk and SBI PO format with 5-8 entities.

questions.stem: Five boxes P, Q, R, S, T are stacked from bottom to top in the order: R, T, P, S, Q. Which box is in the middle (3rd position from the bottom)?

options.option_text: Box P is in the middle (3rd from bottom)
Box S is in the middle (S is 4th from bottom, not 3rd)
Box T is in the middle (T is 2nd from bottom, not 3rd)
Box R is in the middle (R is at the very bottom, 1st position)

questions.explanation: Stack from bottom to top: R(1st), T(2nd), P(3rd), S(4th), Q(5th/top). 3rd from bottom = P. ALSO: 3rd from top = 5−3+1 = 3rd from bottom = P (middle of 5 is symmetric). TOP-BOTTOM TRANSLATION: position from top = (n + 1) − position from bottom, where n = total boxes. For P: from top = (5+1)−3 = 3rd from top ✓ (P is exactly the middle). STEP-BY-STEP for any stacking puzzle: (1) Fix which end is 'bottom' and which is 'top'. (2) List order carefully. (3) Count from required end. EXAM TRAP: confusing 'from bottom' with 'from top' — read the question carefully. PYQ FREQUENCY: basic box arrangement in IBPS Clerk/PO prelims, SBI Clerk prelims — 1 set per paper (5 questions based on 1 arrangement).

questions.stem: A box is 3rd from the top and 4th from the bottom of a stack. What is the total number of boxes in the stack?

options.option_text: 6 boxes in total (3 + 4 − 1 = 6)
7 boxes in total (adding 3 + 4 without subtracting the box itself)
5 boxes in total (subtracting 4 − 3 and adding some value incorrectly)
8 boxes in total (doubling one of the values, an incorrect approach)

questions.explanation: FORMULA: Total = position from top + position from bottom − 1. Here: 3 + 4 − 1 = 6. WHY subtract 1? The box at that position is counted in BOTH 'from top' and 'from bottom' counts — so it is counted twice. Subtracting 1 corrects for double-counting. VISUALISE: Top → [1st][2nd][THIS BOX][4th][5th][6th] ← Bottom. THIS BOX is 3rd from top ✓ and 4th from bottom ✓. Total = 6 ✓. GENERAL FORMULA: Total = (rank from one end) + (rank from other end) − 1. EXAM VARIANTS: (a) Box is 4th from top and 6th from bottom → total = 4+6−1 = 9. (b) Box is kth from top and same rank from bottom → total is odd and = 2k−1. PYQ FREQUENCY: this formula-based shortcut in SSC CGL, IBPS Clerk, RRB NTPC — 1× per paper as a standalone question or clue within a set.

questions.stem: Six boxes are stacked. Box A is at the top. Box B is immediately below A. Box C is at the bottom. Box D is 2nd from the bottom. Box F is immediately above D. Box E is between B and F. Which box is 3rd from the top?

options.option_text: Box E is 3rd from the top
Box F is 3rd from the top (F is 4th from top, not 3rd)
Box B is 3rd from the top (B is 2nd from top, not 3rd)
Box D is 3rd from the top (D is 5th from top, 2nd from bottom)

questions.explanation: SOLVE STEP-BY-STEP: Given 6 boxes. Known fixed positions: A=top(1st), C=bottom(6th), D=2nd from bottom(5th). F immediately above D → F is 4th from top. B immediately below A → B is 2nd from top. E is between B(2nd) and F(4th) → E is 3rd from top. FINAL ARRANGEMENT (top to bottom): A(1), B(2), E(3), F(4), D(5), C(6). VERIFY ALL CLUES: A at top ✓ | B immediately below A ✓ | C at bottom ✓ | D 2nd from bottom ✓ | F immediately above D ✓ | E between B and F ✓. EXAM STRATEGY: always start by fixing the ends (top/bottom), then place items with direct adjacency clues, then fill gaps. PYQ FREQUENCY: 6-box stacking sets in IBPS PO/Clerk prelims, SBI Clerk — appear as 4-5 Q sets; this type in every IBPS exam since 2017.

questions.stem: Seven people sit in a row. Rani is 4th from the left. Suresh is 3 positions to the right of Rani (7th from left). Mohan is 2nd from the right. Priya is immediately to the left of Rani. Kavya is at the leftmost position. Raj is between Kavya and Priya. Deepa occupies the remaining position. How many positions to the right of Kavya is Deepa?

options.option_text: 4 positions to the right of Kavya (Kavya=1st, Deepa=5th; 5−1=4)
3 positions to the right of Kavya (off by one — Deepa is at 5th, not 4th)
5 positions to the right of Kavya (Deepa would be at 6th — that is Mohan's seat)
2 positions to the right of Kavya (Deepa would be at 3rd — that is Priya's seat)

questions.explanation: BUILD THE ARRANGEMENT: Kavya=1, ?, Priya=3, Rani=4, ?, Mohan=6, Suresh=7. Rani 4th ✓. Suresh = Rani+3 = 7th ✓. Mohan = 2nd from right = 7−2+1 = 6th ✓. Priya immediately left of Rani(4) → Priya=3 ✓. Raj between Kavya(1) and Priya(3) → Raj=2. Remaining position=5 → Deepa=5. FINAL (left→right): Kavya(1), Raj(2), Priya(3), Rani(4), Deepa(5), Mohan(6), Suresh(7). ANSWER: Deepa(5) − Kavya(1) = 4 positions to the right ✓. VERIFY: Raj between Kavya(1) and Priya(3) → at 2, which is between them ✓. EXAM TIP: When 7 people are given, place end/fixed positions first, then use adjacency/relative clues, leaving 1 unknown for the remaining slot. PYQ FREQUENCY: 7-person row arrangement in IBPS PO Mains, SBI PO Mains reasoning — 1 full set (5 Qs) per paper.

questions.stem: A 5-floor building (floor 1 = ground, floor 5 = top). Five people: Farhaan, Gauri, Harish, Imran, Jay. Gauri is 2 floors below Farhaan. Harish is on the top floor. Imran is on the 1st floor. Jay is between Farhaan and Imran. Who lives immediately below Farhaan?

options.option_text: Jay lives immediately below Farhaan (Jay=2nd, Farhaan=3rd)
Gauri lives immediately below Farhaan (Gauri is 2 floors below, not 1)
Imran lives immediately below Farhaan (Imran is on 1st floor, far below)
Harish lives immediately below Farhaan (Harish is at the top, above Farhaan)

questions.explanation: SOLVE: Harish=5 (top), Imran=1 (ground). Gauri is 2 floors below Farhaan. Farhaan can be at 3, 4: if Farhaan=4, Gauri=2; if Farhaan=3, Gauri=1=Imran (conflict). So Farhaan=3, Gauri=1 — but Imran=1 too (conflict). Try Farhaan=4: Gauri=2. Jay between Farhaan(4) and Imran(1) → Jay at 2 or 3. But Gauri=2 → Jay=3. FINAL: Imran(1), Gauri(2), Jay(3), Farhaan(4), Harish(5). VERIFY: Gauri(2) is 2 floors below Farhaan(4) ✓ | Jay(3) between Farhaan(4) and Imran(1) ✓ | Harish at top ✓ | Imran at ground ✓. Who is immediately below Farhaan(4)? → Jay at floor 3 ✓. EXAM TRAP: 'Gauri is 2 floors below' ≠ 'Gauri is immediately below'. Difference of 2 means skip one floor — Jay fits in between. PYQ FREQUENCY: 5-floor puzzles in IBPS Clerk prelims, SBI Clerk — very common since 2019.

questions.stem: A 7-floor building. Seven residents: A, B, C, D, E, F, G. E lives on the 7th floor. F lives on the 4th floor. C lives on an even-numbered floor. A lives immediately above B. There are 2 floors between D and G, with D above G. B does not live on the 1st floor. Who lives on the 3rd floor?

options.option_text: D lives on the 3rd floor (D=3, G=1 is the only valid D-G placement)
B lives on the 3rd floor (B=3 is invalid — it forces A=4 which conflicts with F=4)
C lives on the 3rd floor (C must be on an even-numbered floor, not 3rd)
G lives on the 3rd floor (if G=3, then D=5; then no valid slot for A-B pair below A=6)

questions.explanation: SOLVE (E=7, F=4 fixed): A immediately above B, B≠1. A-B pairs (sequential): (3,2), (6,5) [can't use (4,3) — F=4; (5,4) — F=4; (7,6) — E=7]. D-G pairs (D 2 floors above G): (3,1), (5,3), (6,4-taken). Case 1: A=3,B=2 → D-G: (3,1) conflicts A=3; (5,3) conflicts A=3. BOTH fail. Case 2: A=6,B=5 → D-G: (3,1) ✓; (5,3) conflicts B=5. So D=3,G=1. C on even floor: options are 2 and 6 (4=F, 6=A). C=2. All 7 floors: G(1),C(2),D(3),F(4),B(5),A(6),E(7) ✓. VERIFY ALL CLUES: E=7 ✓ | F=4 ✓ | C=2 (even) ✓ | A above B immediately (A=6, B=5) ✓ | D-G apart by 2, D above G (D=3, G=1) ✓ | B≠1 ✓. 3rd floor = D ✓. PYQ FREQUENCY: 7-floor puzzles are the most common format in IBPS PO/Clerk Mains reasoning — typically 4-5 Qs per puzzle set. Appear in SBI PO Mains, RBI Grade-B.

questions.stem: Eight people A–H sit in a row facing North. D is 4th from the left. H is 3rd from the right. B is immediately to the left of D. C is immediately to the right of H. G is at the leftmost position. F is between G and B. A is between D and H. How many people are between B and H?

options.option_text: 2 people (D and A sit between B and H in positions 4 and 5)
3 people (overcounting — only D and A are between positions 3 and 6)
1 person (undercounting — D alone between B and H misses A at position 5)
0 people (wrong — B and H are not adjacent; there are 2 gaps between them)

questions.explanation: BUILD THE ROW: D=4th from left. H=3rd from right=8−3+1=6th from left. B immediately left of D(4) → B=3. C immediately right of H(6) → C=7. G at leftmost → G=1. F between G(1) and B(3) → F=2. A between D(4) and H(6) → A=5. Remaining position 8 → E=8. FINAL (left→right): G(1), F(2), B(3), D(4), A(5), H(6), C(7), E(8). VERIFY: D=4 ✓ | H=6 (3rd from right) ✓ | B immediately left of D ✓ | C immediately right of H ✓ | G leftmost ✓ | F between G and B ✓ | A between D and H ✓. Between B(3) and H(6): positions 4(D) and 5(A) → 2 people ✓. EXAM TIP: for 8-person rows, H=3rd from right means position 6 (not position 3 from left). Always convert 'from right' to 'from left' using (n+1−k). PYQ FREQUENCY: 8-person row puzzles in IBPS PO Mains, SBI PO Mains 2019-2024 — 5 questions per set, typically 1 set per paper.
